extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent examiners (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing the patent 'Abstract of the Disclosure' for U.S. patent applications, including required placement, length, content, language, and examiner actions on defects or missing abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract placement on separate sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief abstract of the technical disclosure in the specification must commence on a separate sheet, preferably following the claims, under the heading "Abstract" or "Abstract of the Disclosure." The sheet or sheets presenting the abstract may not include other parts of the application or other material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. 1.72; Form paragraph 6.16.01 notes the requirement and that it applies to amendments as well as the initial filing. The abstract for a national stage 35 U.S.C. 371 application may appear on the PCT publication front page. Examiner should require a new abstract if it does not commence on a separate sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract heading
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use either "Abstract" or "Abstract of the Disclosure" as a heading for the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred headings are explicitly permitted; ensure heading is present and clearly labels the separate sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must be as concise as the disclosure permits, preferably not exceeding 150 words in length; the abstract should be in narrative form and generally limited to a single paragraph preferably within the range of 50 to 150 words in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exceed 15 lines of text. Abstracts exceeding 15 lines or 150 words should be checked to see if they can be made more concise. The abstract must be as concise as the disclosure permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the abstract is to enable the Office and the public generally to determine quickly from a cursory inspection the nature and gist of the technical disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should sufficiently describe the disclosure to assist readers in deciding whether to consult the full patent text for details. Keep focus on nature/gist rather than exhaustive detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include what is new in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent abstract is a concise statement of the technical disclosure of the patent and should include that which is new in the art to which the invention pertains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is basic in nature, the entire technical disclosure may be new and the abstract should be directed to the entire disclosure; if an improvement, the abstract should include the technical disclosure of the improvement and mention any preferred modifications or alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not state merits, speculative applications, or compare to prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should not refer to purported merits or speculative applications of the invention and should not compare the invention with the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid promotional or evaluative language; keep descriptive and factual about the technical disclosure only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where applicable include key items by invention type
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, the abstract should include the following: (1) if a machine or apparatus, its organization and operation; (2) if an article, its method of making; (3) if a chemical compound, its identity and use; (4) if a mixture, its ingredients; (5) if a process, the steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are illustrative checklists — include the listed element(s) appropriate to the invention type, but avoid extensive mechanical and design details of apparatus. For chemical processes, state type of reaction, reagents and process conditions, generally illustrated by a single example unless variations are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical abstracts: give class and use; exemplify species
rubrics_metrics.description: In chemical patent abstracts for compounds or compositions, the general nature of the compound or composition should be given as well as the use thereof. Exemplification of a species could be illustrative of members of the class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For chemical processes, mention type of reaction, reagents and process conditions and generally illustrate by a single example unless variations are necessary. Example phrasing: "The compounds are of the class of alkyl benzene sulfonyl ureas, useful as oral anti-diabetics."

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extensive mechanical/design detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive mechanical and design details of apparatus should not be included in the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe organization and operation at a high level; exclude detailed dimensions, intricate component descriptions, or implementation particulars that are better left to the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative form, single paragraph, and line limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be in narrative form and generally limited to a single paragraph; the abstract should not exceed 15 lines of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use continuous prose (not bulleted lists or claim-like repetition). Keep it to one paragraph; remodel longer text to concise narrative within the stated word/line ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid claim/legal phraseology and implied phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: The form and legal phraseology often used in patent claims, such as "means" and "said," should be avoided. The abstract should avoid using phrases which can be implied, such as, "This disclosure concerns," "The disclosure defined by this invention," "This disclosure describes," etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain, clear technical language rather than claim-style or boilerplate introductory phrases that add no substantive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not repeat the title
rubrics_metrics.description: The language should be clear and concise and should not repeat information given in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title information that adds nothing to the technical gist should be omitted from the abstract to save space and avoid redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility for preparation; examiner responsibility for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of the abstract is the responsibility of the applicant. The review of the abstract for compliance with these guidelines is the responsibility of the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any necessary amendment to the abstract at allowance or a printer query must be made either by the applicant or by the examiner with applicant's approval (see MPEP § 1302.04). Background knowledge of the art and appreciation of applicant’s contribution are important in preparing the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must require or object to missing/defective abstracts early
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP will review applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) for compliance with 37 CFR 1.72 and will require an abstract if one has not been filed. In all other applications which lack an abstract, the examiner in the first Office action should require the submission of an abstract directed to the technical disclosure; if the abstract does not comply with guidelines, the examiner should point out the defect in the first Office action or at the earliest point in prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 6.12 (Abstract Missing) for missing abstracts and Form Paragraph 6.13 (Abstract Objected To) for objected abstracts; include examiner notes in bracketed areas about informalities (e.g., legal phraseology, undue length).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of replies and formal practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to actions requiring either a new abstract or amendment to bring the abstract into compliance should be treated under 37 CFR 1.111(b) practice like any other formal matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure responses are timely and are processed as formal matters; consider special handling for pro se applicants with follow-on form paragraphs as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check amendments for introduction of new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission of a new abstract or amendment to an existing abstract should be carefully reviewed for introduction of new matter (35 U.S.C. 132, MPEP § 608.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should scrutinize newly submitted or amended abstracts to ensure they do not introduce subject matter beyond the original disclosure; this is especially important because the abstract will be printed on the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract will be printed on the patent; ensure adequacy before issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract will be printed on the patent. Upon passing the application to issue, the examiner should make certain that the abstract is an adequate and clear statement of the contents of the disclosure and generally in line with the guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is otherwise in condition for allowance except for abstract noncompliance, the examiner generally should make necessary revisions by a formal examiner’s amendment after obtaining applicant’s authorization rather than issuing an Ex parte Quayle action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for standardized examiner communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard form paragraphs exist for abstract-related actions: ¶6.12 (Abstract Missing), ¶6.13 (Abstract Objected To), ¶6.14 (Abstract Content reminder), ¶6.15 (Abstract: Chemical Cases), ¶6.16 (Abstract: Language), and ¶6.16.01 (Abstract Placement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should use these form paragraphs where applicable and follow examiner notes (e.g., special handling for pro se applicants, national stage considerations). Form paragraphs include suggested boilerplate text and examiner notes about what to indicate in objections.
